# songsheet: a renderer for chord sheets `songsheet` reads a song written in a small line-based markup from **standard input** and writes it to standard output as aligned plain text or as HTML, optionally transposed. Everything the output depends on is defined here; nothing is read except standard input and the command line. Build and run it as `node src/songsheet.js` (entry point `src/songsheet.js`, CommonJS; other modules go next to it in `src/`). Usage: `songsheet [OPTION...] < song`. Exit status 1 and a single `error:` line on standard output when something is wrong (no other output then), otherwise 0. ## 1. The markup The song is read line by line. Trailing white space of every line is removed first. These line types are recognised, in this order (the first that applies wins): 1. a line that is empty after that, or starts with `//`: ignored. 2. **title** `== TEXT ==` (spaces around `TEXT` optional): the title of the song. A second title is `error: line N: second title`, an empty `TEXT` is `error: line N: empty title`. 3. **meta** `:NAME VALUE`: `NAME` is the first word (case folded to lower case), `VALUE` the rest of the line trimmed; a line without a value is `error: line N: bad meta line`. Meta lines are kept in file order. `:key` takes a key (a note `A`-`G` with optional `#` or `b`, then an optional `m` for minor, e.g. `Em`, `F#`, `Bbm`; else `error: line N: bad key 'VALUE'`); `:capo` takes a number 0 to 11 (else `error: line N: bad capo 'VALUE'`); each of these two may appear once (`error: line N: duplicate 'NAME'`). Any other name is free text. 4. **section** `[[NAME]]` or `[[NAME]] xK` (`K` one digit, 2 to 9: the section is *repeated* `K` times; `x0`, `x1` give `error: line N: bad repeat count`): starts a new section. `NAME` is trimmed. 5. **recall** `>> NAME`: starts a new section called `NAME (again)` that contains a copy of the lines of the most recent earlier section called `NAME` (`error: line N: unknown section 'NAME'` if there is none). Later lines belong to the new section. 6. **note** `!TEXT`: an annotation (`TEXT` trimmed, may be empty). 7. **chord line** `. CHORD CHORD ...` (a dot, then a space or the end of the line): chords only, separated by white space. 8. anything else: a **lyric line** with inline chords written `{CHORD}` (white space inside the braces is trimmed). `\{` and `\}` are a literal brace; a `}` without `{` is an ordinary character; `{` without a closing `}` on the line is `error: line N: unclosed '{'`; `{}` or `{ }` is `error: line N: empty chord`. Lines before the first section belong to an unnamed section. Lines of every kind except title and meta belong to the current section. The first error in file order is the one reported. A lyric line is a list of **segments** `(chord or none, text)`: first the text before the first chord, as a segment without chord (present only if that text is not empty, or if the line has no chords at all, in which case it is the one segment holding the whole line), then, for every chord, a segment with that chord and the text that follows it up to the next chord (possibly empty). ## 2. Chords and transposition A **chord** is a root note `A`-`G` with an optional `#` or `b`, a quality made of letters, digits and `+ # ( ) -` (possibly empty), and optionally `/` and a bass note (root with optional `#`/`b`). Anything else (`N.C.`, `x`, `||`) is not a chord and is never changed by transposition. Notes have semitone numbers `C=0 D=2 E=4 F=5 G=7 A=9 B=11`, `#` adds 1 and `b` subtracts 1, modulo 12 (so `Cb` is `B`, `B#` is `C`). To **transpose** a chord by `S` semitones, move its root (and its bass note, if any) by `S` modulo 12 and keep the quality text. Notes are written with one of two tables: **sharps** `C C# D D# E F F# G G# A A# B`, or **flats** `C Db D Eb E F Gb G Ab A Bb B`. **Which table.** Keys are written as in `:key`. A key is *flat* when it is one of: `F`, `Bb`, `Eb`, `Ab`, `Db`, `Gb`, `Dm`, `Gm`, `Cm`, `Fm`, `Bbm`, `Ebm` (compared by semitone and minor/major, so `A#` is the same key as `Bb`). All other keys are sharp. The table used for the chords is the one of the key the chords are written in, which is the transposed key lowered by the capo number when the song has a capo (see below). If the song has no `:key`, the table is sharps unless `--prefer flats` is given. The `Key:` header line is written with the table of the transposed key itself. ## 3. Options * `--format text|html` (default `text`) * `--transpose N`: shift every chord and the key by `N` semitones (an integer, optional sign, -11 to 11) * `--to KEY`: transpose to `KEY` (a key as in `:key`). Only the root of `KEY` is used: the shift is `(root of KEY - root of the song key) mod 12`, taking 7 to 11 as the negative shifts -5 to -1 (so the shift is between -5 and 6); the song keeps its own major/minor. Needs a `:key` in the song (`error: --to needs a key in the song`, found after the song was read without errors). Cannot be combined with `--transpose`. * `--prefer sharps|flats`: the table to use when the song has no `:key` (default `sharps`) Options come in `NAME VALUE` pairs and are read left to right; the last repeat of an option wins. Option errors are reported before the song is read, the first one wins: `error: unknown option 'X'` (any other word), `error: missing value for --X`, `error: bad value 'V' for --X`; at the end, `error: --transpose and --to cannot be combined` . **Capo.** With `:capo N` (N > 0) the chords are printed as *shapes*: they are shifted down by `N` semitones in addition to any transposition (shift = transposition - N, modulo 12 on the notes). The key (if any) is *not* lowered. The header shows `Capo: N`. ## 4. Text output Lines are produced in this order, one per output line: 1. If there is a title: the title, then a line of `=` as long as the title. 2. The **header lines**: `Key: K` (when the song has a key; `K` is the key after transposition, root written with a table as described above, then `m` if minor), `Capo: N` (when the capo is not 0), then the other meta lines in file order as `Name: value` (the name with its first letter in upper case). 3. For every section, in order: an empty line; then, if the section has a name or a repeat count above 1, its label line: `[NAME]`, followed by ` xK` if the repeat count is `K > 1` (just `xK` if the name is empty); then its lines: * a note: `(note: TEXT)`; * a chord line: the chords (transposed) joined by two spaces; * a lyric line: the lyric (all segment texts joined) preceded, if the line has chords, by the **chord line**: start with an empty string; for each chord, in order, let `col` be the number of lyric characters before it; the chord is placed at column `col`, but at least 1 space after the end of the previous chord (when there is one): pad with spaces to that column and append the chord. The chord line has no trailing spaces; the lyric is printed as it is (not shifted). If the lyric is empty or only white space after removing the chords, only the chord line is printed; a lyric line without chords is printed as it is (an empty one gives an empty line). There is no trailing blank line and no blank line after the last section. ## 5. HTML output One element per output line, exactly in this form (`ESC(x)` replaces `&` by `&`, `<` by `<`, `>` by `>`, `"` by `"`, in this order of treatment of a character, nothing else): ```

ESC(title)

(only with a title)

ESC(header line)

(one per header line of the text output, same text)

ESC(label)

(only with a name or repeat count > 1; label as in the text output without brackets) ...lines...
``` `SLUG` is the section name in lower case with every run of characters other than `a-z0-9` replaced by one `-`, and leading and trailing `-` removed; `section` if that leaves nothing. The label for the `

` is the name, followed by ` xK` for a repeat count above 1, trimmed of white space at both ends. Lines inside a section: * note: `

ESC(text)

`; * chord line: `

ESC(chords joined by one space)

` (chords transposed); * lyric line without chords: `

ESC(text)

`; * lyric line with chords: `

` followed by one `ESC(chord)ESC(text)` per segment (the chord transposed; for a segment without chord the `` element is empty), then `

`. Segments without chord and with empty text do not occur. ## 6. Examples `songsheet` reading this on standard input: ``` == Tin Roof Rain == :key Dm :tempo 96 [[Bridge]] !tacet old light river hold {Bb/D}& lonely !half time & soft walking again roa{Eb}d <3 // a comment [[Outro]] road {Dm}lonely {Am}& bells {Gm}sky <3 loud sky {Dm}light found {Am}I ``` prints: ``` Tin Roof Rain ============= Key: Dm Tempo: 96 [Bridge] (note: tacet) Bb/D old light river hold & lonely (note: half time & soft) Eb walking again road <3 [Outro] Dm Am Gm road lonely & bells sky <3 Dm Am loud sky light found I ``` `songsheet --format html` reading this on standard input: ``` == Orchard Waltz == :key G :artist Mira Vale [[Outro]] loud {D}ringing bells again sky harbour {Am}sky singing {G}<3 a >> Outro [[Intro]] {D7}friend sky {Bb/D}"quote" {Am}"quote" bells loud !tacet a ringing {Em}winter {Em}{C} >> Intro [[Chorus]] x3 ! {Bm}{C} // a comment ``` prints: ```

D7friend sky A#/D"quote" Am"quote" bells loud

# chordwright: a renderer for chord sheets `chordwright` reads a song written in a small line-based markup from **standard input** and writes it to standard output as aligned plain text or as HTML, optionally transposed. Everything the output depends on is defined here; nothing is read except standard input and the command line. Build and run it as `python3 src/chordwright.py` (entry point `src/chordwright.py`; other modules go next to it in `src/`). Usage: `chordwright [OPTION...] < song`. Exit status 1 and a single `error:` line on standard output when something is wrong (no other output then), otherwise 0. ## 1. The markup The song is read line by line. Trailing white space of every line is removed first. These line types are recognised, in this order (the first that applies wins): 1. a line that is empty after that, or starts with `//`: ignored. 2. **title** `== TEXT ==` (spaces around `TEXT` optional): the title of the song. A second title is `error: line N: second title`, an empty `TEXT` is `error: line N: empty title`. 3. **meta** `:NAME VALUE`: `NAME` is the first word (case folded to lower case), `VALUE` the rest of the line trimmed; a line without a value is `error: line N: bad meta line`. Meta lines are kept in file order. `:key` takes a key (a note `A`-`G` with optional `#` or `b`, then an optional `m` for minor, e.g. `Em`, `F#`, `Bbm`; else `error: line N: bad key 'VALUE'`); `:capo` takes a number 0 to 11 (else `error: line N: bad capo 'VALUE'`); each of these two may appear once (`error: line N: duplicate 'NAME'`). Any other name is free text. 4. **section** `[[NAME]]`: starts a new section. `NAME` is trimmed. (A repeat suffix such as `x2` is not supported here: `error: line N: repeat marks are not supported`.) 5. **recall** `>> NAME`: starts a new section called `NAME (again)` that contains a copy of the lines of the most recent earlier section called `NAME` (`error: line N: unknown section 'NAME'` if there is none). Later lines belong to the new section. 6. **note** `!TEXT`: an annotation (`TEXT` trimmed, may be empty). 7. **chord line** `. CHORD CHORD ...` (a dot, then a space or the end of the line): chords only, separated by white space. 8. anything else: a **lyric line** with inline chords written `{CHORD}` (white space inside the braces is trimmed). `\{` and `\}` are a literal brace; a `}` without `{` is an ordinary character; `{` without a closing `}` on the line is `error: line N: unclosed '{'`; `{}` or `{ }` is `error: line N: empty chord`. Lines before the first section belong to an unnamed section. Lines of every kind except title and meta belong to the current section. The first error in file order is the one reported. A lyric line is a list of **segments** `(chord or none, text)`: first the text before the first chord, as a segment without chord (present only if that text is not empty, or if the line has no chords at all, in which case it is the one segment holding the whole line), then, for every chord, a segment with that chord and the text that follows it up to the next chord (possibly empty). ## 2. Chords and transposition A **chord** is a root note `A`-`G` with an optional `#` or `b`, a quality made of letters, digits and `+ # ( ) -` (possibly empty), and optionally `/` and a bass note (root with optional `#`/`b`). Anything else (`N.C.`, `x`, `||`) is not a chord and is never changed by transposition. Notes have semitone numbers `C=0 D=2 E=4 F=5 G=7 A=9 B=11`, `#` adds 1 and `b` subtracts 1, modulo 12 (so `Cb` is `B`, `B#` is `C`). To **transpose** a chord by `S` semitones, move its root (and its bass note, if any) by `S` modulo 12 and keep the quality text. Notes are written with one of two tables: **sharps** `C C# D D# E F F# G G# A A# B`, or **flats** `C Db D Eb E F Gb G Ab A Bb B`. **Which table.** Keys are written as in `:key`. A key is *flat* when it is one of: `F`, `Bb`, `Eb`, `Ab`, `Dm`, `Gm`, `Cm`, `Fm` (compared by semitone and minor/major, so `A#` is the same key as `Bb`). All other keys are sharp. The table used for the chords is the one of the key the chords are written in, i.e. the transposed key. If the song has no `:key`, the table is sharps. The `Key:` header line is written with the same table as the chords. ## 3. Options * `--format text|html` (default `text`) * `--transpose N`: shift every chord and the key by `N` semitones (an integer, optional sign, -11 to 11) * `--to KEY`: transpose to `KEY` (a key as in `:key`). Only the root of `KEY` is used: the shift is `(root of KEY - root of the song key) mod 12`, taking 7 to 11 as the negative shifts -5 to -1 (so the shift is between -5 and 6); the song keeps its own major/minor. Needs a `:key` in the song (`error: --to needs a key in the song`, found after the song was read without errors). Cannot be combined with `--transpose`. Options come in `NAME VALUE` pairs and are read left to right; the last repeat of an option wins. Option errors are reported before the song is read, the first one wins: `error: unknown option 'X'` (any other word), `error: missing value for --X`, `error: bad value 'V' for --X`; at the end, `error: --transpose and --to cannot be combined` . **Capo.** `:capo N` is information only: the header shows `Capo: N` (when `N` is not 0) and the chords are not changed. ## 4. Text output Lines are produced in this order, one per output line: 1. If there is a title: the title, then a line of `=` as long as the title. 2. The **header lines**: `Key: K` (when the song has a key; `K` is the key after transposition, root written with a table as described above, then `m` if minor), `Capo: N` (when the capo is not 0), then the other meta lines in file order as `Name: value` (the name with its first letter in upper case). 3. For every section, in order: an empty line; then, if the section has a name or a repeat count above 1, its label line: `[NAME]`, followed by ` xK` if the repeat count is `K > 1` (just `xK` if the name is empty); then its lines: * a note: `(note: TEXT)`; * a chord line: the chords (transposed) joined by two spaces; * a lyric line: the lyric (all segment texts joined) preceded, if the line has chords, by the **chord line**: start with an empty string; for each chord, in order, let `col` be the number of lyric characters before it; the chord is placed at column `col`, but at least 2 spaces after the end of the previous chord (when there is one): pad with spaces to that column and append the chord. The chord line has no trailing spaces; the lyric is printed as it is (not shifted). If the lyric is empty or only white space after removing the chords, only the chord line is printed; a lyric line without chords is printed as it is (an empty one gives an empty line). There is no trailing blank line and no blank line after the last section. ## 5. HTML output One element per output line, exactly in this form (`ESC(x)` replaces `&` by `&`, `<` by `<`, `>` by `>`, `"` by `"`, in this order of treatment of a character, nothing else): ```

ESC(title)

(only with a title)

ESC(header line)

(one per header line of the text output, same text)

ESC(label)

(only with a name or repeat count > 1; label as in the text output without brackets) ...lines...
``` `SLUG` is the section name in lower case with every run of characters other than `a-z0-9` replaced by one `-`, and leading and trailing `-` removed; `section` if that leaves nothing. The label for the `

# lyricforge: a renderer for chord sheets `lyricforge` reads a song written in a small line-based markup from **standard input** and writes it to standard output as aligned plain text or as HTML, optionally transposed. Everything the output depends on is defined here; nothing is read except standard input and the command line. Build and run it as `node src/lyricforge.js` (entry point `src/lyricforge.js`, CommonJS; other modules go next to it in `src/`). Usage: `lyricforge [OPTION...] < song`. Exit status 1 and a single `error:` line on standard output when something is wrong (no other output then), otherwise 0. ## 1. The markup The song is read line by line. Trailing white space of every line is removed first. These line types are recognised, in this order (the first that applies wins): 1. a line that is empty after that, or starts with `//`: ignored. 2. **title** `== TEXT ==` (spaces around `TEXT` optional): the title of the song. A second title is `error: line N: second title`, an empty `TEXT` is `error: line N: empty title`. 3. **meta** `:NAME VALUE`: `NAME` is the first word (case folded to lower case), `VALUE` the rest of the line trimmed; a line without a value is `error: line N: bad meta line`. Meta lines are kept in file order. `:key` takes a key (a note `A`-`G` with optional `#` or `b`, then an optional `m` for minor, e.g. `Em`, `F#`, `Bbm`; else `error: line N: bad key 'VALUE'`); `:capo` takes a number 0 to 11 (else `error: line N: bad capo 'VALUE'`); each of these two may appear once (`error: line N: duplicate 'NAME'`). Any other name is free text. 4. **section** `[[NAME]]` or `[[NAME]] xK` (`K` one digit, 2 to 9: the section is *repeated* `K` times; `x0`, `x1` give `error: line N: bad repeat count`): starts a new section. `NAME` is trimmed. 5. a line starting with `>>`: `error: line N: recall is not supported`. 6. **note** `!TEXT`: an annotation (`TEXT` trimmed, may be empty). 7. **chord line** `. CHORD CHORD ...` (a dot, then a space or the end of the line): chords only, separated by white space. 8. anything else: a **lyric line** with inline chords written `{CHORD}` (white space inside the braces is trimmed). `\{` and `\}` are a literal brace; a `}` without `{` is an ordinary character; `{` without a closing `}` on the line is `error: line N: unclosed '{'`; `{}` or `{ }` is `error: line N: empty chord`. Lines before the first section belong to an unnamed section. Lines of every kind except title and meta belong to the current section. The first error in file order is the one reported. A lyric line is a list of **segments** `(chord or none, text)`: first the text before the first chord, as a segment without chord (present only if that text is not empty, or if the line has no chords at all, in which case it is the one segment holding the whole line), then, for every chord, a segment with that chord and the text that follows it up to the next chord (possibly empty). ## 2. Chords and transposition A **chord** is a root note `A`-`G` with an optional `#` or `b`, a quality made of letters, digits and `+ # ( ) -` (possibly empty), and optionally `/` and a bass note (root with optional `#`/`b`). Anything else (`N.C.`, `x`, `||`) is not a chord and is never changed by transposition. Notes have semitone numbers `C=0 D=2 E=4 F=5 G=7 A=9 B=11`, `#` adds 1 and `b` subtracts 1, modulo 12 (so `Cb` is `B`, `B#` is `C`). To **transpose** a chord by `S` semitones, move its root (and its bass note, if any) by `S` modulo 12 and keep the quality text. Notes are written with one of two tables: **sharps** `C C# D D# E F F# G G# A A# B`, or **flats** `C Db D Eb E F Gb G Ab A Bb B`. **Which table.** Keys are written as in `:key`. A key is *flat* when it is one of: `F`, `Bb`, `Eb`, `Ab`, `Db`, `Dm`, `Gm`, `Cm`, `Fm`, `Bbm` (compared by semitone and minor/major, so `A#` is the same key as `Bb`). All other keys are sharp. The table used for the chords is the one of the key the chords are written in, which is the transposed key lowered by the capo number when the song has a capo (see below). If the song has no `:key`, the table is sharps unless `--prefer flats` is given. The `Key:` header line is written with the table of the transposed key itself. ## 3. Options * `--format text|html` (default `text`) * `--transpose N`: shift every chord and the key by `N` semitones (an integer, optional sign, -11 to 11) * `--prefer sharps|flats`: the table to use when the song has no `:key` (default `sharps`) Options come in `NAME VALUE` pairs and are read left to right; the last repeat of an option wins. Option errors are reported before the song is read, the first one wins: `error: unknown option 'X'` (any other word), `error: missing value for --X`, `error: bad value 'V' for --X` . **Capo.** With `:capo N` (N > 0) the chords are printed as *shapes*: they are shifted down by `N` semitones in addition to any transposition (shift = transposition - N, modulo 12 on the notes). The key (if any) is *not* lowered. The header shows `Capo: N`. ## 4. Text output Lines are produced in this order, one per output line: 1. If there is a title: the title, then a line of `=` as long as the title. 2. The **header lines**: `Key: K` (when the song has a key; `K` is the key after transposition, root written with a table as described above, then `m` if minor), `Capo: N` (when the capo is not 0), then the other meta lines in file order as `Name: value` (the name with its first letter in upper case). 3. For every section, in order: an empty line; then, if the section has a name or a repeat count above 1, its label line: `[NAME]`, followed by ` xK` if the repeat count is `K > 1` (just `xK` if the name is empty); then its lines: * a note: `(note: TEXT)`; * a chord line: the chords (transposed) joined by two spaces; * a lyric line: the lyric (all segment texts joined) preceded, if the line has chords, by the **chord line**: start with an empty string; for each chord, in order, let `col` be the number of lyric characters before it; the chord is placed at column `col`, but at least 1 space after the end of the previous chord (when there is one): pad with spaces to that column and append the chord. The chord line has no trailing spaces; the lyric is printed as it is (not shifted). If the lyric is empty or only white space after removing the chords, only the chord line is printed; a lyric line without chords is printed as it is (an empty one gives an empty line). There is no trailing blank line and no blank line after the last section. ## 5. HTML output One element per output line, exactly in this form (`ESC(x)` replaces `&` by `&`, `<` by `<`, `>` by `>`, `"` by `"`, in this order of treatment of a character, nothing else): ```

ESC(title)

(only with a title)

ESC(header line)

(one per header line of the text output, same text)

ESC(label)

(only with a name or repeat count > 1; label as in the text output without brackets) ...lines...
``` `SLUG` is the section name in lower case with every run of characters other than `a-z0-9` replaced by one `-`, and leading and trailing `-` removed; `section` if that leaves nothing. The label for the `

ESC(text)

`; * chord line: `

ESC(chords joined by one space)

` (chords transposed); * lyric line without chords: `

ESC(text)

`; * lyric line with chords: `

` followed by one `ESC(chord)ESC(text)` per segment (the chord transposed; for a segment without chord the `` element is empty), then `

`. Segments without chord and with empty text do not occur. ## 6. F C F !tacet light bells ho{F#m7b5}me on "quote" [[Outro]] x2 !slowly home {C7}morning hold {C7}harbour {Eb}hold stone friend ``` prints: ``` The Long Way Round ================== Key: F [Bridge] Am C7 on bells lonely ringing & Dm C7 I walking loud old Dm harbour tight hold ringing [Intro] C C C7 Gbm7b5 ringing on <3 loud tight on home friend [Bridge] Bb C7 F road found on the road F C F (note: tacet) Gbm7b5 light bells home on "quote" [Outro] x2 (note: slowly) C7 C7 Eb home morning hold harbour hold stone friend ``` `lyricforge --format html` reading this on standard input: ``` == Salt & Pepper Moon == :key Em :tempo The Tin Roofs [[Chorus]] {Bm}home walking {C}road h{F#m7b5}ome found singing . start.README.md:
# strummer: a renderer for chord sheets `strummer` reads a song written in a small line-based markup from **standard input** and writes it to standard output as aligned plain text or as HTML, optionally transposed. Everything the output depends on is defined here; nothing is read except standard input and the command line. Build and run it as `python3 src/strummer.py` (entry point `src/strummer.py`; other modules go next to it in `src/`). Usage: `strummer [OPTION...] < song`. Exit status 1 and a single `error:` line on standard output when something is wrong (no other output then), otherwise 0. ## 1. The markup The song is read line by line. Trailing white space of every line is removed first. These line types are recognised, in this order (the first that applies wins): 1. a line that is empty after that, or starts with `//`: ignored. 2. **title** `== TEXT ==` (spaces around `TEXT` optional): the title of the song. A second title is `error: line N: second title`, an empty `TEXT` is `error: line N: empty title`. 3. **meta** `:NAME VALUE`: `NAME` is the first word (case folded to lower case), `VALUE` the rest of the line trimmed; a line without a value is `error: line N: bad meta line`. Meta lines are kept in file order. `:key` takes a key (a note `A`-`G` with optional `#` or `b`, then an optional `m` for minor, e.g. `Em`, `F#`, `Bbm`; else `error: line N: bad key 'VALUE'`); `:capo` takes a number 0 to 11 (else `error: line N: bad capo 'VALUE'`); each of these two may appear once (`error: line N: duplicate 'NAME'`). Any other name is free text. 4. **section** `[[NAME]]` or `[[NAME]] xK` (`K` one digit, 2 to 9: the section is *repeated* `K` times; `x0`, `x1` give `error: line N: bad repeat count`): starts a new section. `NAME` is trimmed. 5. **recall** `>> NAME`: starts a new section called `NAME (again)` that contains a copy of the lines of the most recent earlier section called `NAME` (`error: line N: unknown section 'NAME'` if there is none). Later lines belong to the new section. 6. **note** `!TEXT`: an annotation (`TEXT` trimmed, may be empty). 7. **chord line** `. CHORD CHORD ...` (a dot, then a space or the end of the line): chords only, separated by white space. 8. anything else: a **lyric line** with inline chords written `{CHORD}` (white space inside the braces is trimmed). `\{` and `\}` are a literal brace; a `}` without `{` is an ordinary character; `{` without a closing `}` on the line is `error: line N: unclosed '{'`; `{}` or `{ }` is `error: line N: empty chord`. Lines before the first section belong to an unnamed section. Lines of every kind except title and meta belong to the current section. The first error in file order is the one reported. A lyric line is a list of **segments** `(chord or none, text)`: first the text before the first chord, as a segment without chord (present only if that text is not empty, or if the line has no chords at all, in which case it is the one segment holding the whole line), then, for every chord, a segment with that chord and the text that follows it up to the next chord (possibly empty). ## 2. Chords and transposition A **chord** is a root note `A`-`G` with an optional `#` or `b`, a quality made of letters, digits and `+ # ( ) -` (possibly empty), and optionally `/` and a bass note (root with optional `#`/`b`). Anything else (`N.C.`, `x`, `||`) is not a chord and is never changed by transposition. Notes have semitone numbers `C=0 D=2 E=4 F=5 G=7 A=9 B=11`, `#` adds 1 and `b` subtracts 1, modulo 12 (so `Cb` is `B`, `B#` is `C`). To **transpose** a chord by `S` semitones, move its root (and its bass note, if any) by `S` modulo 12 and keep the quality text. Notes are written with one of two tables: **sharps** `C C# D D# E F F# G G# A A# B`, or **flats** `C Db D Eb E F Gb G Ab A Bb B`. **Which table.** Keys are written as in `:key`. A key is *flat* when it is one of: `F`, `Bb`, `Eb`, `Dm`, `Gm`, `Cm`, `Am`, `Em` (compared by semitone and minor/major, so `A#` is the same key as `Bb`). All other keys are sharp. The table used for the chords is the one of the key the chords are written in, which is the transposed key lowered by the capo number when the song has a capo (see below). If the song has no `:key`, the table is sharps. The `Key:` header line is written with the same table as the chords. ## 3. Options * `--format text|html` (default `text`) * `--transpose N`: shift every chord and the key by `N` semitones (an integer, optional sign, -11 to 11) * `--to KEY`: transpose to `KEY` (a key as in `:key`). Only the root of `KEY` is used: the shift is `(root of KEY - root of the song key) mod 12`, taking 7 to 11 as the negative shifts -5 to -1 (so the shift is between -5 and 6); the song keeps its own major/minor. Needs a `:key` in the song (`error: --to needs a key in the song`, found after the song was read without errors). Cannot be combined with `--transpose`. Options come in `NAME VALUE` pairs and are read left to right; the last repeat of an option wins. Option errors are reported before the song is read, the first one wins: `error: unknown option 'X'` (any other word), `error: missing value for --X`, `error: bad value 'V' for --X`; at the end, `error: --transpose and --to cannot be combined` . **Capo.** With `:capo N` (N > 0) the chords are printed as *shapes*: they are shifted down by `N` semitones in addition to any transposition (shift = transposition - N, modulo 12 on the notes). The key (if any) is *not* lowered. The header shows `Capo: N`. ## 4. Text output Lines are produced in this order, one per output line: 1. If there is a title: the title, then a line of `=` as long as the title. 2. The **header lines**: `Key: K` (when the song has a key; `K` is the key after transposition, root written with a table as described above, then `m` if minor), `Capo: N` (when the capo is not 0), then the other meta lines in file order as `Name: value` (the name with its first letter in upper case). 3. For every section, in order: an empty line; then, if the section has a name or a repeat count above 1, its label line: `[NAME]`, followed by ` xK` if the repeat count is `K > 1` (just `xK` if the name is empty); then its lines: * a note: `(note: TEXT)`; * a chord line: the chords (transposed) joined by two spaces; * a lyric line: the lyric (all segment texts joined) preceded, if the line has chords, by the **chord line**: start with an empty string; for each chord, in order, let `col` be the number of lyric characters before it; the chord is placed at column `col`, but at least 2 spaces after the end of the previous chord (when there is one): pad with spaces to that column and append the chord. The chord line has no trailing spaces; the lyric is printed as it is (not shifted). If the lyric is empty or only white space after removing the chords, only the chord line is printed; a lyric line without chords is printed as it is (an empty one gives an empty line). There is no trailing blank line and no blank line after the last section. ## 5. HTML output One element per output line, exactly in this form (`ESC(x)` replaces `&` by `&`, `<` by `<`, `>` by `>`, `"` by `"`, in this order of treatment of a character, nothing else): ```

ESC(title)

(only with a title)

ESC(header line)

(one per header line of the text output, same text)

ESC(label)

(only with a name or repeat count > 1; label as in the text output without brackets) ...lines...
``` `SLUG` is the section name in lower case with every run of characters other than `a-z0-9` replaced by one `-`, and leading and trailing `-` removed; `section` if that leaves nothing. The label for the `

ESC(text)

`; * chord line: `

ESC(chords joined by one space)

` (chords transposed); * lyric line without chords: `

ESC(text)

`; * lyric line with chords: `

` followed by one `ESC(chord)ESC(text)` per segment (the chord transposed; for a segment without chord the `` element is empty), then `

`. Segments without chord and with empty text do not occur. ## 6. # capotool: a renderer for chord sheets `capotool` reads a song written in a small line-based markup from **standard input** and writes it to standard output as aligned plain text or as HTML, optionally transposed. Everything the output depends on is defined here; nothing is read except standard input and the command line. Build and run it as `node src/capotool.js` (entry point `src/capotool.js`, CommonJS; other modules go next to it in `src/`). Usage: `capotool [OPTION...] < song`. Exit status 1 and a single `error:` line on standard output when something is wrong (no other output then), otherwise 0. ## 1. The markup The song is read line by line. Trailing white space of every line is removed first. These line types are recognised, in this order (the first that applies wins): 1. a line that is empty after that, or starts with `//`: ignored. 2. **title** `== TEXT ==` (spaces around `TEXT` optional): the title of the song. A second title is `error: line N: second title`, an empty `TEXT` is `error: line N: empty title`. 3. **meta** `:NAME VALUE`: `NAME` is the first word (case folded to lower case), `VALUE` the rest of the line trimmed; a line without a value is `error: line N: bad meta line`. Meta lines are kept in file order. `:key` takes a key (a note `A`-`G` with optional `#` or `b`, then an optional `m` for minor, e.g. `Em`, `F#`, `Bbm`; else `error: line N: bad key 'VALUE'`); `:capo` takes a number 0 to 11 (else `error: line N: bad capo 'VALUE'`); each of these two may appear once (`error: line N: duplicate 'NAME'`). Any other name is free text. 4. **section** `[[NAME]]`: starts a new section. `NAME` is trimmed. (A repeat suffix such as `x2` is not supported here: `error: line N: repeat marks are not supported`.) 5. **recall** `>> NAME`: starts a new section called `NAME (again)` that contains a copy of the lines of the most recent earlier section called `NAME` (`error: line N: unknown section 'NAME'` if there is none). Later lines belong to the new section. 6. **note** `!TEXT`: an annotation (`TEXT` trimmed, may be empty). 7. **chord line** `. CHORD CHORD ...` (a dot, then a space or the end of the line): chords only, separated by white space. 8. anything else: a **lyric line** with inline chords written `{CHORD}` (white space inside the braces is trimmed). `\{` and `\}` are a literal brace; a `}` without `{` is an ordinary character; `{` without a closing `}` on the line is `error: line N: unclosed '{'`; `{}` or `{ }` is `error: line N: empty chord`. Lines before the first section belong to an unnamed section. Lines of every kind except title and meta belong to the current section. The first error in file order is the one reported. A lyric line is a list of **segments** `(chord or none, text)`: first the text before the first chord, as a segment without chord (present only if that text is not empty, or if the line has no chords at all, in which case it is the one segment holding the whole line), then, for every chord, a segment with that chord and the text that follows it up to the next chord (possibly empty). ## 2. Chords and transposition A **chord** is a root note `A`-`G` with an optional `#` or `b`, a quality made of letters, digits and `+ # ( ) -` (possibly empty), and optionally `/` and a bass note (root with optional `#`/`b`). Anything else (`N.C.`, `x`, `||`) is not a chord and is never changed by transposition. Notes have semitone numbers `C=0 D=2 E=4 F=5 G=7 A=9 B=11`, `#` adds 1 and `b` subtracts 1, modulo 12 (so `Cb` is `B`, `B#` is `C`). To **transpose** a chord by `S` semitones, move its root (and its bass note, if any) by `S` modulo 12 and keep the quality text. Notes are written with one of two tables: **sharps** `C C# D D# E F F# G G# A A# B`, or **flats** `C Db D Eb E F Gb G Ab A Bb B`. **Which table.** Keys are written as in `:key`. A key is *flat* when it is one of: `Bb`, `Eb`, `Ab`, `Db`, `Gb`, `Gm`, `Cm`, `Fm`, `Bbm`, `Ebm`, `Abm` (compared by semitone and minor/major, so `A#` is the same key as `Bb`). All other keys are sharp. The table used for the chords is the one of the key the chords are written in, i.e. the transposed key. If the song has no `:key`, the table is sharps unless `--prefer flats` is given. The `Key:` header line is written with the same table as the chords. ## 3. Options * `--format text|html` (default `text`) * `--transpose N`: shift every chord and the key by `N` semitones (an integer, optional sign, -11 to 11) * `--to KEY`: transpose to `KEY` (a key as in `:key`). Only the root of `KEY` is used: the shift is `(root of KEY - root of the song key) mod 12`, taking 7 to 11 as the negative shifts -5 to -1 (so the shift is between -5 and 6); the song keeps its own major/minor. Needs a `:key` in the song (`error: --to needs a key in the song`, found after the song was read without errors). Cannot be combined with `--transpose`. * `--prefer sharps|flats`: the table to use when the song has no `:key` (default `sharps`) Options come in `NAME VALUE` pairs and are read left to right; the last repeat of an option wins. Option errors are reported before the song is read, the first one wins: `error: unknown option 'X'` (any other word), `error: missing value for --X`, `error: bad value 'V' for --X`; at the end, `error: --transpose and --to cannot be combined` . **Capo.** `:capo N` is information only: the header shows `Capo: N` (when `N` is not 0) and the chords are not changed. ## 4. Text output Lines are produced in this order, one per output line: 1. If there is a title: the title, then a line of `=` as long as the title. 2. The **header lines**: `Key: K` (when the song has a key; `K` is the key after transposition, root written with a table as described above, then `m` if minor), `Capo: N` (when the capo is not 0), then the other meta lines in file order as `Name: value` (the name with its first letter in upper case). 3. For every section, in order: an empty line; then, if the section has a name or a repeat count above 1, its label line: `[NAME]`, followed by ` xK` if the repeat count is `K > 1` (just `xK` if the name is empty); then its lines: * a note: `(note: TEXT)`; * a chord line: the chords (transposed) joined by two spaces; * a lyric line: the lyric (all segment texts joined) preceded, if the line has chords, by the **chord line**: start with an empty string; for each chord, in order, let `col` be the number of lyric characters before it; the chord is placed at column `col`, but at least 1 space after the end of the previous chord (when there is one): pad with spaces to that column and append the chord. The chord line has no trailing spaces; the lyric is printed as it is (not shifted). If the lyric is empty or only white space after removing the chords, only the chord line is printed; a lyric line without chords is printed as it is (an empty one gives an empty line). There is no trailing blank line and no blank line after the last section. ## 5. HTML output One element per output line, exactly in this form (`ESC(x)` replaces `&` by `&`, `<` by `<`, `>` by `>`, `"` by `"`, in this order of treatment of a character, nothing else): ```

ESC(title)

(only with a title)

ESC(header line)

(one per header line of the text output, same text)

ESC(label)

(only with a name or repeat count > 1; label as in the text output without brackets) ...lines...
``` `SLUG` is the section name in lower case with every run of characters other than `a-z0-9` replaced by one `-`, and leading and trailing `-` removed; `section` if that leaves nothing. The label for the `

` is the name, followed by ` xK` for a repeat count above 1, trimmed of white space at both ends. Lines inside a section: * note: `

ESC(text)

`; * chord line: `

ESC(chords joined by one space)

` (chords transposed); * lyric line without chords: `

ESC(text)

`; * lyric line with chords: `

` followed by one `ESC(chord)ESC(text)` per segment (the chord transposed; for a segment without chord the `` element is empty), then `

`. Segments without chord and with empty text do not occur. ## 6. Examples `capotool` reading this on standard input: ``` == Tin Roof Rain == :key F :year 96 [[Intro]] ho{Am}ld hold under {C7}tight {C}harbour light {Bb}under {Gm}again {C7}on winter home morning {Bb}{C7} [[Pre-Chorus (soft)]] under hom{Am}e {F}loud old {Am}sky stone {Dsus4}walking on {C7}under friend {Am}on !half time & soft ``` prints: ``` Tin Roof Rain ============= Key: F Year: 96 [Intro] Am C7 C A# hold hold under tight harbour light under Gm C7 again on winter home morning A# C7 [Pre-Chorus (soft)] Am F Am Dsus4 under home loud old sky stone walking C7 Am on under friend on (note: half time & soft) ``` `capotool --format html` reading this on standard input: ``` == Salt & Pepper Moon == :key D [[Pre-Chorus (soft)]] light hold {Em}the {A7}friend {Em}morning the {G}harbour {F#m}down on {A}home [[Intro]] <3 friend bells river {Bm}river morning ston{Em}e loud found roa{Bm}d {Em}river li{Bb/D}ght {A}I on {D}tight {Eb}walking wi{Bm}nter >> Pre-Chorus (soft) // a comment ``` prints: ```

start.README.md:
# tabloid: a renderer for chord sheets `tabloid` reads a song written in a small line-based markup from **standard input** and writes it to standard output as aligned plain text or as HTML, optionally transposed. Everything the output depends on is defined here; nothing is read except standard input and the command line. Build and run it as `python3 src/tabloid.py` (entry point `src/tabloid.py`; other modules go next to it in `src/`). Usage: `tabloid [OPTION...] < song`. Exit status 1 and a single `error:` line on standard output when something is wrong (no other output then), otherwise 0. ## 1. The markup The song is read line by line. Trailing white space of every line is removed first. These line types are recognised, in this order (the first that applies wins): 1. a line that is empty after that, or starts with `//`: ignored. 2. **title** `== TEXT ==` (spaces around `TEXT` optional): the title of the song. A second title is `error: line N: second title`, an empty `TEXT` is `error: line N: empty title`. 3. **meta** `:NAME VALUE`: `NAME` is the first word (case folded to lower case), `VALUE` the rest of the line trimmed; a line without a value is `error: line N: bad meta line`. Meta lines are kept in file order. `:key` takes a key (a note `A`-`G` with optional `#` or `b`, then an optional `m` for minor, e.g. `Em`, `F#`, `Bbm`; else `error: line N: bad key 'VALUE'`); `:capo` takes a number 0 to 11 (else `error: line N: bad capo 'VALUE'`); each of these two may appear once (`error: line N: duplicate 'NAME'`). Any other name is free text. 4. **section** `[[NAME]]` or `[[NAME]] xK` (`K` one digit, 2 to 9: the section is *repeated* `K` times; `x0`, `x1` give `error: line N: bad repeat count`): starts a new section. `NAME` is trimmed. 5. a line starting with `>>`: `error: line N: recall is not supported`. 6. **note** `!TEXT`: an annotation (`TEXT` trimmed, may be empty). 7. **chord line** `. CHORD CHORD ...` (a dot, then a space or the end of the line): chords only, separated by white space. 8. anything else: a **lyric line** with inline chords written `{CHORD}` (white space inside the braces is trimmed). `\{` and `\}` are a literal brace; a `}` without `{` is an ordinary character; `{` without a closing `}` on the line is `error: line N: unclosed '{'`; `{}` or `{ }` is `error: line N: empty chord`. Lines before the first section belong to an unnamed section. Lines of every kind except title and meta belong to the current section. The first error in file order is the one reported. A lyric line is a list of **segments** `(chord or none, text)`: first the text before the first chord, as a segment without chord (present only if that text is not empty, or if the line has no chords at all, in which case it is the one segment holding the whole line), then, for every chord, a segment with that chord and the text that follows it up to the next chord (possibly empty). ## 2. Chords and transposition A **chord** is a root note `A`-`G` with an optional `#` or `b`, a quality made of letters, digits and `+ # ( ) -` (possibly empty), and optionally `/` and a bass note (root with optional `#`/`b`). Anything else (`N.C.`, `x`, `||`) is not a chord and is never changed by transposition. Notes have semitone numbers `C=0 D=2 E=4 F=5 G=7 A=9 B=11`, `#` adds 1 and `b` subtracts 1, modulo 12 (so `Cb` is `B`, `B#` is `C`). To **transpose** a chord by `S` semitones, move its root (and its bass note, if any) by `S` modulo 12 and keep the quality text. Notes are written with one of two tables: **sharps** `C C# D D# E F F# G G# A A# B`, or **flats** `C Db D Eb E F Gb G Ab A Bb B`. **Which table.** Keys are written as in `:key`. A key is *flat* when it is one of: `F`, `Bb`, `Eb`, `Ab`, `Db`, `Gb`, `Dm`, `Gm`, `Cm`, `Fm` (compared by semitone and minor/major, so `A#` is the same key as `Bb`). All other keys are sharp. The table used for the chords is the one of the key the chords are written in, which is the transposed key lowered by the capo number when the song has a capo (see below). If the song has no `:key`, the table is sharps unless `--prefer flats` is given. The `Key:` header line is written with the table of the transposed key itself. ## 3. Options * `--format text|html` (default `text`) * `--transpose N`: shift every chord and the key by `N` semitones (an integer, optional sign, -11 to 11) * `--prefer sharps|flats`: the table to use when the song has no `:key` (default `sharps`) Options come in `NAME VALUE` pairs and are read left to right; the last repeat of an option wins. Option errors are reported before the song is read, the first one wins: `error: unknown option 'X'` (any other word), `error: missing value for --X`, `error: bad value 'V' for --X` . **Capo.** With `:capo N` (N > 0) the chords are printed as *shapes*: they are shifted down by `N` semitones in addition to any transposition (shift = transposition - N, modulo 12 on the notes). The key (if any) is *not* lowered. The header shows `Capo: N`. ## 4. Text output Lines are produced in this order, one per output line: 1. If there is a title: the title, then a line of `=` as long as the title. 2. The **header lines**: `Key: K` (when the song has a key; `K` is the key after transposition, root written with a table as described above, then `m` if minor), `Capo: N` (when the capo is not 0), then the other meta lines in file order as `Name: value` (the name with its first letter in upper case). 3. For every section, in order: an empty line; then, if the section has a name or a repeat count above 1, its label line: `[NAME]`, followed by ` xK` if the repeat count is `K > 1` (just `xK` if the name is empty); then its lines: * a note: `(note: TEXT)`; * a chord line: the chords (transposed) joined by two spaces; * a lyric line: the lyric (all segment texts joined) preceded, if the line has chords, by the **chord line**: start with an empty string; for each chord, in order, let `col` be the number of lyric characters before it; the chord is placed at column `col`, but at least 1 space after the end of the previous chord (when there is one): pad with spaces to that column and append the chord. The chord line has no trailing spaces; the lyric is printed as it is (not shifted). If the lyric is empty or only white space after removing the chords, only the chord line is printed; a lyric line without chords is printed as it is (an empty one gives an empty line). There is no trailing blank line and no blank line after the last section. ## 5. HTML output One element per output line, exactly in this form (`ESC(x)` replaces `&` by `&`, `<` by `<`, `>` by `>`, `"` by `"`, in this order of treatment of a character, nothing else): ```

ESC(title)

(only with a title)

ESC(header line)

(one per header line of the text output, same text)

ESC(label)

(only with a name or repeat count > 1; label as in the text output without brackets) ...lines...
``` `SLUG` is the section name in lower case with every run of characters other than `a-z0-9` replaced by one `-`, and leading and trailing `-` removed; `section` if that leaves nothing. The label for the `

ESC(text)

`. Segments without chord and with empty text do not occur. ## 6. # setlister: a renderer for chord sheets `setlister` reads a song written in a small line-based markup from **standard input** and writes it to standard output as aligned plain text or as HTML, optionally transposed. Everything the output depends on is defined here; nothing is read except standard input and the command line. Build and run it as `node src/setlister.js` (entry point `src/setlister.js`, CommonJS; other modules go next to it in `src/`). Usage: `setlister [OPTION...] < song`. Exit status 1 and a single `error:` line on standard output when something is wrong (no other output then), otherwise 0. ## 1. The markup The song is read line by line. Trailing white space of every line is removed first. These line types are recognised, in this order (the first that applies wins): 1. a line that is empty after that, or starts with `//`: ignored. 2. **title** `== TEXT ==` (spaces around `TEXT` optional): the title of the song. A second title is `error: line N: second title`, an empty `TEXT` is `error: line N: empty title`. 3. **meta** `:NAME VALUE`: `NAME` is the first word (case folded to lower case), `VALUE` the rest of the line trimmed; a line without a value is `error: line N: bad meta line`. Meta lines are kept in file order. `:key` takes a key (a note `A`-`G` with optional `#` or `b`, then an optional `m` for minor, e.g. `Em`, `F#`, `Bbm`; else `error: line N: bad key 'VALUE'`); `:capo` takes a number 0 to 11 (else `error: line N: bad capo 'VALUE'`); each of these two may appear once (`error: line N: duplicate 'NAME'`). Any other name is free text. 4. **section** `[[NAME]]` or `[[NAME]] xK` (`K` one digit, 2 to 9: the section is *repeated* `K` times; `x0`, `x1` give `error: line N: bad repeat count`): starts a new section. `NAME` is trimmed. 5. **recall** `>> NAME`: starts a new section called `NAME (again)` that contains a copy of the lines of the most recent earlier section called `NAME` (`error: line N: unknown section 'NAME'` if there is none). Later lines belong to the new section. 6. **note** `!TEXT`: an annotation (`TEXT` trimmed, may be empty). 7. **chord line** `. CHORD CHORD ...` (a dot, then a space or the end of the line): chords only, separated by white space. 8. anything else: a **lyric line** with inline chords written `{CHORD}` (white space inside the braces is trimmed). `\{` and `\}` are a literal brace; a `}` without `{` is an ordinary character; `{` without a closing `}` on the line is `error: line N: unclosed '{'`; `{}` or `{ }` is `error: line N: empty chord`. Lines before the first section belong to an unnamed section. Lines of every kind except title and meta belong to the current section. The first error in file order is the one reported. A lyric line is a list of **segments** `(chord or none, text)`: first the text before the first chord, as a segment without chord (present only if that text is not empty, or if the line has no chords at all, in which case it is the one segment holding the whole line), then, for every chord, a segment with that chord and the text that follows it up to the next chord (possibly empty). ## 2. Chords and transposition A **chord** is a root note `A`-`G` with an optional `#` or `b`, a quality made of letters, digits and `+ # ( ) -` (possibly empty), and optionally `/` and a bass note (root with optional `#`/`b`). Anything else (`N.C.`, `x`, `||`) is not a chord and is never changed by transposition. Notes have semitone numbers `C=0 D=2 E=4 F=5 G=7 A=9 B=11`, `#` adds 1 and `b` subtracts 1, modulo 12 (so `Cb` is `B`, `B#` is `C`). To **transpose** a chord by `S` semitones, move its root (and its bass note, if any) by `S` modulo 12 and keep the quality text. Notes are written with one of two tables: **sharps** `C C# D D# E F F# G G# A A# B`, or **flats** `C Db D Eb E F Gb G Ab A Bb B`. **Which table.** Keys are written as in `:key`. A key is *flat* when it is one of: `F`, `Bb`, `Ab`, `Dm`, `Gm`, `Fm` (compared by semitone and minor/major, so `A#` is the same key as `Bb`). All other keys are sharp. The table used for the chords is the one of the key the chords are written in, which is the transposed key lowered by the capo number when the song has a capo (see below). If the song has no `:key`, the table is sharps. The `Key:` header line is written with the same table as the chords. ## 3. Options * `--format text|html` (default `text`) * `--transpose N`: shift every chord and the key by `N` semitones (an integer, optional sign, -11 to 11) Options come in `NAME VALUE` pairs and are read left to right; the last repeat of an option wins. Option errors are reported before the song is read, the first one wins: `error: unknown option 'X'` (any other word), `error: missing value for --X`, `error: bad value 'V' for --X` . **Capo.** With `:capo N` (N > 0) the chords are printed as *shapes*: they are shifted down by `N` semitones in addition to any transposition (shift = transposition - N, modulo 12 on the notes). The key (if any) is *not* lowered. The header shows `Capo: N`. ## 4. Text output Lines are produced in this order, one per output line: 1. If there is a title: the title, then a line of `=` as long as the title. 2. The **header lines**: `Key: K` (when the song has a key; `K` is the key after transposition, root written with a table as described above, then `m` if minor), `Capo: N` (when the capo is not 0), then the other meta lines in file order as `Name: value` (the name with its first letter in upper case). 3. For every section, in order: an empty line; then, if the section has a name or a repeat count above 1, its label line: `[NAME]`, followed by ` xK` if the repeat count is `K > 1` (just `xK` if the name is empty); then its lines: * a note: `(note: TEXT)`; * a chord line: the chords (transposed) joined by two spaces; * a lyric line: the lyric (all segment texts joined) preceded, if the line has chords, by the **chord line**: start with an empty string; for each chord, in order, let `col` be the number of lyric characters before it; the chord is placed at column `col`, but at least 2 spaces after the end of the previous chord (when there is one): pad with spaces to that column and append the chord. The chord line has no trailing spaces; the lyric is printed as it is (not shifted). If the lyric is empty or only white space after removing the chords, only the chord line is printed; a lyric line without chords is printed as it is (an empty one gives an empty line). There is no trailing blank line and no blank line after the last section. ## 5. HTML output One element per output line, exactly in this form (`ESC(x)` replaces `&` by `&`, `<` by `<`, `>` by `>`, `"` by `"`, in this order of treatment of a character, nothing else): ```

ESC(title)

(only with a title)

ESC(header line)

(one per header line of the text output, same text)

ESC(label)

(only with a name or repeat count > 1; label as in the text output without brackets) ...lines...
``` `SLUG` is the section name in lower case with every run of characters other than `a-z0-9` replaced by one `-`, and leading and trailing `-` removed; `section` if that leaves nothing. The label for the `

` is the name, followed by ` xK` for a repeat count above 1, trimmed of white space at both ends. Lines inside a section: * note: `

ESC(text)

`; * chord line: `

ESC(chords joined by one space)

` (chords transposed); * lyric line without chords: `

ESC(text)

`; * lyric line with chords: `

` followed by one `ESC(chord)ESC(text)` per segment (the chord transposed; for a segment without chord the `` element is empty), then `

`. Segments without chord and with empty text do not occur. ## 6. Examples `setlister` reading this on standard input: ``` == Salt & Pepper Moon == :key G [[Outro]] . C D N.C. {Am}stone on {Bm}tight {G}singing home {D7}walking harbour {Em}road [[Pre-Chorus (soft)]] x4 light walking the "quote" home sto{C}ne old loud a {D7}{Am} // a comment ``` prints: ``` Salt & Pepper Moon ================== Key: G [Outro] C D N.C. Am Bm G stone on tight singing home D7 Em walking harbour road [Pre-Chorus (soft)] x4 light walking the "quote" C home stone old loud a D7 Am ``` `setlister --format html` reading this on standard input: ``` == Orchard Waltz == :key E :tempo 96 [[Intro]] I {F#m7b5}light sky {B7}again sky the {B}ringing {B7}old I again >> Intro // a comment [[Verse 1]] x3 . x2 N.C. walking river {F#m}again lonely {F#m}a on the walking river lonely singing [[Verse 1]] x4 {C#7#9}stone tight {C#m}"quote" {C#m}tight {G#m}bells tight I {Bb/D}winter und{E}er {G#m}& stone {B7}lonely singing ``` prints: ```

# fretwork: a renderer for chord sheets `fretwork` reads a song written in a small line-based markup from **standard input** and writes it to standard output as aligned plain text or as HTML, optionally transposed. Everything the output depends on is defined here; nothing is read except standard input and the command line. Build and run it as `python3 src/fretwork.py` (entry point `src/fretwork.py`; other modules go next to it in `src/`). Usage: `fretwork [OPTION...] < song`. Exit status 1 and a single `error:` line on standard output when something is wrong (no other output then), otherwise 0. ## 1. The markup The song is read line by line. Trailing white space of every line is removed first. These line types are recognised, in this order (the first that applies wins): 1. a line that is empty after that, or starts with `//`: ignored. 2. **title** `== TEXT ==` (spaces around `TEXT` optional): the title of the song. A second title is `error: line N: second title`, an empty `TEXT` is `error: line N: empty title`. 3. **meta** `:NAME VALUE`: `NAME` is the first word (case folded to lower case), `VALUE` the rest of the line trimmed; a line without a value is `error: line N: bad meta line`. Meta lines are kept in file order. `:key` takes a key (a note `A`-`G` with optional `#` or `b`, then an optional `m` for minor, e.g. `Em`, `F#`, `Bbm`; else `error: line N: bad key 'VALUE'`); `:capo` takes a number 0 to 11 (else `error: line N: bad capo 'VALUE'`); each of these two may appear once (`error: line N: duplicate 'NAME'`). Any other name is free text. 4. **section** `[[NAME]]`: starts a new section. `NAME` is trimmed. (A repeat suffix such as `x2` is not supported here: `error: line N: repeat marks are not supported`.) 5. a line starting with `>>`: `error: line N: recall is not supported`. 6. **note** `!TEXT`: an annotation (`TEXT` trimmed, may be empty). 7. **chord line** `. CHORD CHORD ...` (a dot, then a space or the end of the line): chords only, separated by white space. 8. anything else: a **lyric line** with inline chords written `{CHORD}` (white space inside the braces is trimmed). `\{` and `\}` are a literal brace; a `}` without `{` is an ordinary character; `{` without a closing `}` on the line is `error: line N: unclosed '{'`; `{}` or `{ }` is `error: line N: empty chord`. Lines before the first section belong to an unnamed section. Lines of every kind except title and meta belong to the current section. The first error in file order is the one reported. A lyric line is a list of **segments** `(chord or none, text)`: first the text before the first chord, as a segment without chord (present only if that text is not empty, or if the line has no chords at all, in which case it is the one segment holding the whole line), then, for every chord, a segment with that chord and the text that follows it up to the next chord (possibly empty). ## 2. Chords and transposition A **chord** is a root note `A`-`G` with an optional `#` or `b`, a quality made of letters, digits and `+ # ( ) -` (possibly empty), and optionally `/` and a bass note (root with optional `#`/`b`). Anything else (`N.C.`, `x`, `||`) is not a chord and is never changed by transposition. Notes have semitone numbers `C=0 D=2 E=4 F=5 G=7 A=9 B=11`, `#` adds 1 and `b` subtracts 1, modulo 12 (so `Cb` is `B`, `B#` is `C`). To **transpose** a chord by `S` semitones, move its root (and its bass note, if any) by `S` modulo 12 and keep the quality text. Notes are written with one of two tables: **sharps** `C C# D D# E F F# G G# A A# B`, or **flats** `C Db D Eb E F Gb G Ab A Bb B`. **Which table.** Keys are written as in `:key`. A key is *flat* when it is one of: `F`, `Bb`, `Eb`, `Ab`, `Db`, `Gb`, `Dm`, `Gm`, `Cm`, `Fm`, `Bbm`, `Ebm`, `Abm` (compared by semitone and minor/major, so `A#` is the same key as `Bb`). All other keys are sharp. The table used for the chords is the one of the key the chords are written in, i.e. the transposed key. If the song has no `:key`, the table is sharps unless `--prefer flats` is given. The `Key:` header line is written with the table of the transposed key itself. ## 3. Options * `--format text|html` (default `text`) * `--transpose N`: shift every chord and the key by `N` semitones (an integer, optional sign, -11 to 11) * `--to KEY`: transpose to `KEY` (a key as in `:key`). Only the root of `KEY` is used: the shift is `(root of KEY - root of the song key) mod 12`, taking 7 to 11 as the negative shifts -5 to -1 (so the shift is between -5 and 6); the song keeps its own major/minor. Needs a `:key` in the song (`error: --to needs a key in the song`, found after the song was read without errors). Cannot be combined with `--transpose`. * `--prefer sharps|flats`: the table to use when the song has no `:key` (default `sharps`) Options come in `NAME VALUE` pairs and are read left to right; the last repeat of an option wins. Option errors are reported before the song is read, the first one wins: `error: unknown option 'X'` (any other word), `error: missing value for --X`, `error: bad value 'V' for --X`; at the end, `error: --transpose and --to cannot be combined` . **Capo.** `:capo N` is information only: the header shows `Capo: N` (when `N` is not 0) and the chords are not changed. ## 4. Text output Lines are produced in this order, one per output line: 1. If there is a title: the title, then a line of `=` as long as the title. 2. The **header lines**: `Key: K` (when the song has a key; `K` is the key after transposition, root written with a table as described above, then `m` if minor), `Capo: N` (when the capo is not 0), then the other meta lines in file order as `Name: value` (the name with its first letter in upper case). 3. For every section, in order: an empty line; then, if the section has a name or a repeat count above 1, its label line: `[NAME]`, followed by ` xK` if the repeat count is `K > 1` (just `xK` if the name is empty); then its lines: * a note: `(note: TEXT)`; * a chord line: the chords (transposed) joined by two spaces; * a lyric line: the lyric (all segment texts joined) preceded, if the line has chords, by the **chord line**: start with an empty string; for each chord, in order, let `col` be the number of lyric characters before it; the chord is placed at column `col`, but at least 2 spaces after the end of the previous chord (when there is one): pad with spaces to that column and append the chord. The chord line has no trailing spaces; the lyric is printed as it is (not shifted). If the lyric is empty or only white space after removing the chords, only the chord line is printed; a lyric line without chords is printed as it is (an empty one gives an empty line). There is no trailing blank line and no blank line after the last section. ## 5.
